sentences.text: A secondary analysis of a longitudinal cohort examined employment status among working-age individuals in a national database, tracking their work status at 1, 2, 5, and 10 years after brain injury.

Statistical modeling identified pre-injury employment as the strongest factor associated with work at every follow-up, with those employed at the time of injury showing higher odds of working at 1, 2, and 5 years.

Employment at 1, 2, or 5 years was associated with a higher chance of being employed at all later time points, whereas being married was only associated with higher employment odds at the one-year mark.

Additionally, the ability to travel independently was linked to a higher chance of employment, while greater functional limitations were associated with a lower chance of working at all measured time points.
